title: Email Marketing for Dog Groomers: Permission First

facts.fact: Under Australia's Spam Act, a business needs the person's consent before sending marketing messages.
facts.quote: Under Australia’s [Spam Act](https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A01214/latest/text), you need consent before you send marketing messages.

facts.fact: Every marketing message under the Spam Act must say who it is from and how to contact the sender, and must include a working unsubscribe.
facts.quote: Every message must say who it’s from and how to contact you, and every one needs a working unsubscribe.

facts.fact: Express consent, the clearest form, means the person knowingly agrees to receive marketing emails, and the sender should keep a record of who said yes, when, and how.
facts.quote: Keep a record of who said yes, when and how. If it’s ever questioned, it’s up to you to show the consent.

facts.fact: The page states that the ACMA considers inferred consent less reliable than express consent, and that inferred consent does not cover someone who has only bought once.
facts.quote: But the ACMA says it’s less reliable than express consent, and it doesn’t cover someone who has simply bought from you once.

facts.fact: Sending an email that asks a client for marketing consent is itself a marketing message.
facts.quote: One thing you can’t do: send an email asking for consent. That request is a marketing message itself.

facts.fact: A past booking does not count as permission to send marketing emails.
facts.quote: A past booking isn’t permission by itself. Ask on your form or at pick-up; you can’t email to ask.

facts.fact: Unsubscribe requests should be acted on within five working days, and the person should be kept off the list even when tools change.
facts.quote: Act on it within five working days and keep them off your list, even when you change tools.

facts.fact: The opt-in box should be left unticked and kept separate from booking terms so that consent is a real choice.
facts.quote: Leave the box unticked, and keep it separate from your booking terms, so it’s a real choice.

facts.fact: The ACMA lists automatically adding people to an email list after a one-off purchase or an enquiry as a common mistake businesses make.
facts.quote: The ACMA lists adding people automatically after a one-off purchase or an enquiry as one of the common mistakes

facts.fact: Before importing an old client spreadsheet into an email tool, every address should be checked, and anyone without clear consent or who has ever unsubscribed should be left out.
facts.quote: Before you import an old client spreadsheet into an email tool, check every address. Leave out anyone without clear consent, and anyone who has ever unsubscribed.

facts.fact: The article is posted with the date 11 March 2026 (written as 11/03/2026 in the page's post stamp).
